Judge: A is better in all four pairs, and none of the margins is close. The A frames look like a shipped AAA title. Glossy clear-coat cars, worn, rusted and grimy surfaces that hint at a story, realistic people, and strong backlit late-day light with haze that deepens with distance give every A shot depth and a cinematic look. All four A frames genuinely wow. The B frames (one Singapore-set build with the same 'Harbour Relay' HUD and a placeholder grid minimap) are not wows. At street level they hold up best: pair 1 has the best crowd and traffic density of all eight images and a decent warm key light. But the pieces at the centre of each frame fall short: a smeared player car, a stylised toy-like protagonist and a low-detail helicopter. The surfaces are clean and look newly built, with no wear. From the air the build falls apart: flat, washed-out haze, boxy uniform towers, flat green and sand ground with scattered identical trees, and no traffic. These two aerial frames (pairs 3 and 4) read as a scale model, and that is the widest gap. The comparison was not fully blind: pair 3 A shows a GTA V logo, and every B shows the same in-development HUD. Pair 1 A also uses a bumper-height camera rather than the '2 m up' in its scene description, while B matches it.
